method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025' (published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026)), 24 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS <license> element for PMC12819074 (Europe PMC returned 503 on 2026-09-23)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438) 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension' (published August 2020), 12 claims; LICENCE: No open licence: the PMC record states 'This file is available for text mining. It may also be used consistent with the principles of fair use under the copyright law.' (free to read; copyright retained) (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC7486815). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every Japan Endocrine Society 2025 claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, the European Society of Hypertension 2020 position statement, paraphrased because it has no open licence. S2 adds Western metanephrine-first testing, phenoxybenzamine (the PBS drug) against doxazosin, somatostatin-receptor PET imaging, post-operative follow-up and metastatic treatment. Its tables (interfering drugs, radiopharmaceuticals, genes) were stripped. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 3 (drugs and foods that affect catecholamine tests), Table 4 (imaging strengths and limits) and Table 5 (triggers of hypertensive crisis) are paraphrased from the row lines. S1 Tables 6-7 and all four S2 tables were not extracted (merged cells).

claims.claim: **About 83% of tumours are adrenal (phaeochromocytoma) and 17% extra-adrenal (paraganglioma);** metastatic disease is 10–15% overall and about three times more frequent in paraganglioma. Incidence is about 5 per million person-years and rising with incidental detection.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Catecholamine excess** causes headache, palpitations, sweating and wide blood pressure swings, and can present as chest pain, takotsubo-type cardiomyopathy, acute heart failure, pulmonary oedema or shock.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Who to test (ESH):** suggestive symptoms, whether spontaneous or triggered by drugs; cardiovascular events such as takotsubo cardiomyopathy with suggestive features; any adrenal incidentaloma of 10 HU or more, hypertensive or not; lean people (BMI under 25) with type 2 diabetes; carriers of a susceptibility-gene variant or those with syndromic features; and anyone with a personal or family history of PPGL.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Screen as an outpatient** using any one of: free metanephrines in plasma above the reference limit; creatinine-corrected metanephrines in a random urine sample more than three times the limit; or blood catecholamines more than three times the limit. (1B)
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If screening is positive, confirm with** a 24-hour urine collection (metanephrines more than three times, or catecholamines more than two times, the reference limit) or plasma free metanephrines; combine biochemistry with imaging because some tumours secrete little. (1B)
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sample carefully:** exercise, stress, posture, temperature, venepuncture, foods and drugs alter results. For plasma metanephrines, fast, lie supine 20–30 minutes and freeze within 30 minutes of separation, or false positives are common. Most antihypertensives do not interfere.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ESH (Western practice) tests first with free normetanephrine and metanephrine in plasma or urine, preferably by LC-MS/MS:** both exclude PPGL with a negative predictive value over 99% at about 94% specificity, and plasma is better in high-risk patients (incidentaloma or surveillance). Add plasma 3-methoxytyramine for dopamine-producing, SDHx or possibly metastatic tumours.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Draw plasma after at least 20 minutes lying down, fasting and without strenuous exercise** (24-hour urinary free metanephrines if that is not possible). A rise more than two-fold above the cut-off, or in two or more metabolites, justifies imaging; smaller single rises need weighing against pre-test risk, and a clonidine suppression test can help.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High-dose dexamethasone can trigger a hypertensive crisis:** use glucocorticoids cautiously when PPGL is suspected.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Image to locate, stage and look for metastases:** CT for primary tumours and lung or liver deposits; MRI for head and neck paraganglioma, adrenal cortical differentiation, and in children or when repeated scans are needed. 123I-MIBG is highly specific; 18F-FDG PET is better for metastases, especially with SDHx variants.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ESH imaging choices:** 68Ga-DOTA-somatostatin-analogue PET is first choice for head and neck paraganglioma, suspected SDH-related tumours and metastatic disease; 18F-FDOPA PET suits VHL or HIF2A tumours; 123I-MIBG is a fallback when PET is not available. Functional imaging is advised to exclude metastases in phaeochromocytomas over 5.0 cm and with SDHA/B/D variants.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Drugs and foods that can distort catecholamine results (S1 Table 3):** tricyclic antidepressants, levodopa, adrenergic agonists such as decongestant nasal sprays (naphazoline, tramazoline), many psychotropics (buspirone, for example), prochlorperazine, clonidine withdrawal, alcohol, amphetamines and metoclopramide; and caffeinated coffee, bananas, citrus, vanilla-flavoured foods, tyramine-rich cheese and red wine.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imaging strengths and limits (S1 Table 4):** CT offers high spatial resolution and a typical pattern (unenhanced attenuation above 10 HU, dense arterial enhancement with late washout); MRI typically shows low T1 and high T2 signal without loss on opposed-phase imaging; neither is specific, so adrenal cancer and metastasis must be excluded. 123I-MIBG is specific and surveys the whole body but is less sensitive, especially in metastatic and SDHx-variant disease; 111In-octreotide is specific and still sensitive with SDHx variants, though low in resolution; 18F-FDG PET is sensitive but non-specific; 18F-FDOPA PET is specific and sensitive even in metastatic and SDHx disease but is not approved in Japan.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Block catecholamine effects adequately before surgery (and in non-operated functional tumours)** to control blood pressure and prevent cardiovascular events. Surgery can release catecholamines, causing crisis, arrhythmia, ischaemia, pulmonary oedema and organ failure. (1C)
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Begin alpha-blockade 7 to 14 days or more ahead of the operation** and titrate to blood pressure and heart rate targets. The guideline's first choice is a selective alpha-1 blocker (1B), adding a calcium channel blocker or metyrosine if needed (2C); non-selective alpha-blockers give better intraoperative haemodynamics, without a difference in complications or deaths.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Doxazosin (long-acting):** begin 1–2 mg/day at bedtime (first-dose postural hypotension) and increase every 2–3 days up to 16 mg until the target is reached.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Phenoxybenzamine (non-selective, non-competitive; the PBS drug) and doxazosin (alpha1-selective) are the usual choices,** both given twice daily, started 7 to 14 days or more before the operation and increased gradually to target. In the only randomised trial, time outside the blood pressure target during surgery did not differ, but phenoxybenzamine gave more haemodynamic stability. Normotensive patients should also be blocked.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Calcium channel blockers can be added to an alpha-blocker,** but are not advised alone unless blood pressure is normal or only mildly raised, or alpha-blockade causes severe orthostatic hypotension. Metyrosine is usually combined with an alpha-blocker; it is hard to obtain and sedating.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never start a beta-blocker before the alpha-blocker** (risk of hypertensive attack; 1A). Add one several days after adequate alpha-blockade for tachycardia, arrhythmia, heart failure or ischaemic heart disease. Avoid labetalol and carvedilol because their beta effect is too strong.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Proposed targets:** seated blood pressure under 130/80 mmHg, standing systolic at least 90 mmHg, heart rate 60–70 bpm seated and 70–80 bpm standing.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Restore blood volume:** a normal-salt diet (9 g/day) from day three of alpha-blockade (plasma volume takes 7–14 days to rise), then 1–2 L of saline from the evening before surgery.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Metyrosine** (catecholamine synthesis inhibitor) helps when alpha-blockade is not enough, e.g. catecholamine cardiomyopathy: start 0.5 g/day, usual 2–3 g/day, maximum 4 g/day. It causes drowsiness, extrapyramidal effects and diarrhoea; patients must drink at least 2 L/day to avoid crystalluria.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surgical removal is first-line (1A):** laparoscopic or robot-assisted adrenalectomy for small phaeochromocytomas (1B), open surgery for large or invasive tumours (2C). Consider partial adrenalectomy in familial disease with high bilateral risk (2C).
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After resection, watch for severe hypotension and hypoglycaemia:** manage in ICU with frequent blood pressure, heart rate and glucose checks; monitor glucose for 48 hours, especially in patients on diabetes drugs. Treat hypotension with fluids and vasopressors.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Head and neck paragangliomas:** block symptomatic patients before surgery; completely asymptomatic ones may be exempted (weak evidence). When radical resection is unsafe, options include wait-and-scan, stereotactic radiosurgery, conventional radiotherapy or somatostatin-receptor-targeted radionuclide therapy, decided by a multidisciplinary team.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Check metanephrines (and 3-methoxytyramine where raised before) two to six weeks after surgery;** normal values confirm complete resection and no imaging is needed. If they stay high, or the tumour was non-functional, image at 3 and 6 months.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **ESH follow-up: everyone for the first ten years,** because recurrence runs at about 1 per 100 person-years and doubles in genetic disease: yearly examination and metanephrines for functional tumours, imaging every two years for non-functional ones. High-risk patients (large tumours, paraganglioma, childhood onset, multifocal disease, SDHB) need stricter yearly checks including 3-methoxytyramine.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Triggers of hypertensive crisis (S1 Table 5).** Daily life: bending over, exercise, a blow to the abdomen, overeating, tyramine-rich food (aged cheese, red wine), alcohol, sneezing, passing urine or stool, stress, smoking and pregnancy. Procedures: abdominal palpation, enemas, tumour biopsy and iodinated contrast. Drugs: dopamine antagonists such as metoclopramide (contraindicated by mouth and by injection; domperidone needs similar caution), glucagon, a beta-blocker on its own, tricyclics, SNRIs, MAO inhibitors and dexamethasone above 2 mg. Other treatments: CVD chemotherapy, 131I-MIBG or external radiotherapy, arterial embolisation, ablation and contrast media.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypertensive crisis (3–11% incidence, about 15% mortality) needs hospital admission:** give intravenous phentolamine, then a continuous infusion, adding calcium channel blockers or nitrates as needed; switch to oral doxazosin once stable. (1B)
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Initial aim:** diastolic pressure at or under 110 mmHg, then about 160/100 mmHg within 2–6 hours. Phentolamine-induced tachycardia is treated with an oral beta-blocker.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In pregnancy, untreated PPGL is highly lethal for mother and baby:** image with ultrasound or MRI; use a selective alpha-blocker (plus nifedipine or amlodipine if needed); if removing the tumour before delivery, operate in the second trimester, no later than 24 weeks.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **20–40% of PPGL is hereditary:** take a detailed family history, tell every patient about genetic testing, and test after genetic counselling (the US and European guidelines advise testing everyone). SDHB variants carry a 35–75% metastatic risk.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow-up:** lifelong after surgery for hereditary PPGL; at least 10 years for sporadic tumours at high recurrence risk (noradrenaline-dominant, 5 cm or larger, or paraganglioma outside the head and neck). Metastasis occurs in 10–15% of phaeochromocytomas and 35–70% of paragangliomas.
claims.locator: Japan Endocrine Society, Endocrine Journal, 'Japan Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma 2025', published online 10 October 2025 (issue 6 January 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12819074/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ESH genetics:** up to 40% carry a germline variant, so consider testing every patient (shared decision), using a targeted next-generation sequencing panel; SDHB carries the highest metastatic risk (30–70%). Offer relatives cascade testing, from age 5 for VHL and SDHB and from 10 for SDHA, SDHC and SDHD.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **About 10–20% develop metastases.** Before treating, stage the disease and show progression (usually imaging over 3 months), unless there are many liver, lung or brain deposits. Rapid progression: chemotherapy, e.g. CVD (cyclophosphamide, vincristine, dacarbazine), with responses up to 70% in SDHx carriers against 30% in sporadic disease.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderately progressive metastatic disease: consider radionuclide therapy with 177Lu-DOTATATE or 131I-MIBG;** external beam radiotherapy is for painful bone lesions or threatened cord compression. Lifelong follow-up with yearly metanephrines and re-staging imaging, more often if the burden is high.
claims.locator: Lenders JWM, Kerstens MN, Amar L, Prejbisz A, et al., Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), Journal of Hypertension 2020;38(8):1443-1456 (doi 10.1097/HJH.0000000000002438), 'Genetics, diagnosis, management and future directions of research of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension', published August 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7486815/, retrieved 2026-09-24
